WORKSHEET · CLASS 30 · AGES 4 YEARS

Fox’s Logic Picnic Worksheet for Age 4

Age 4 YearsClass 30 · LogicType Printable PDFPlays with <a href="/preschool/logic/adventures/foxs-logic-picnic/">the online game</a>

A puzzle piece AND a food name one basket each — match both clues to find Fox’s picnic baskets.

On the sheet: Use the clues to find the right picnic basket!

THE ACTUAL WORKSHEET

Exactly what you’ll print.

This is the real sheet — the same file the buttons above hand you. Title, instructions, the activity itself, and a grown-up answer line where it helps.

Download Free Worksheet ↓ Play This Activity Online ↗

The PDF is a real printable file (A4, prints fine on US Letter). The print button prints only the worksheet — never the website around it. No sign-up, nothing stored.

ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

This is two-clue deduction: neither clue alone picks the basket. The piece gives the colour, the food gives the contents, and each row offers one right-colour-wrong-food and one right-food-wrong-colour basket — so both clues must be used. Saying it aloud (“green… and an apple… so the green apple basket!”) is the whole skill.

  • Two-clue deduction
  • Colour and content matching
  • Rejecting near-misses
  • Explaining an answer
HOW TO USE IT

Three easy steps.

  1. Say the rule first

    Every puzzle has a rule — a pattern, a size order, two clues together. Say it aloud before solving, and the sheet solves itself.

  2. Point before circling

    Have your child point at the answer and say why, then circle it. The pointing keeps the thinking honest.

  3. Check together with the answer line

    The grown-up answer strip at the bottom lets you check without guessing — and lets your child play teacher.

TEACHING TIPS

Little things that help.

Sort real things too

After the sorting sheets, sort socks or spoons the same way. Real objects make the rule permanent.

Patterns everywhere

Lay out apple-grape-apple snacks and ask what comes next. The sheet teaches the skill; the kitchen keeps it.

Mazes build pencil control too

The maze sheet doubles as pencil practice — slow and steady on the path matters more than speed.

Answer guide

Clue 1 = the green basket with an apple. Clue 2 = the yellow basket with a cupcake. Clue 3 = the red basket with a cookie. Every other basket breaks exactly one clue — ask which one!

WHERE THIS FITS

The class and the game behind it.

This worksheet is the paper twin of Fox’s Logic Picnic, a real game in the Logic Adventures library. It belongs to Logic, Thinking & Problem-Solving (Class 30) on the Age 4 learning path, and the whole logic collection lives at /worksheets/logic/. Play the game on screen first, print the worksheet second — or the other way round; they practice the same skill in two languages.
